correctness.rationale: The source's Lemma B.1 reduces positive endemic equilibria to positive roots of the scalar function \(F\). Direct differentiation shows strict monotonicity in both \(\beta_1\) and \(\beta_2\) for every positive \(I\). A fresh symbolic calculation verified the package derivative simplification and, after substituting the source thresholds, verified identically that the cleared corner value equals a negative positive-prefactor times \(I^2(C_0+C_1I)\). Under \(0<\sigma\le1\), both \(C_0\) and \(C_1\) are positive. Thus the corner is strictly negative for all \(I>0\), and monotonicity propagates this to the claimed rectangle.
risks: The theorem excludes endemic equilibria only; it does not prove global convergence to the disease-free equilibrium.

value.rationale: The theorem closes an explicit gap between the source's proved backward-bifurcation regime and its numerical complementary regime. It sharply separates the existence of endemic equilibria from the stronger, still-unproved global-convergence claim and settles the threshold boundary as well.

final_claim: For the Khan--Wang--Liu--Xiong SEIRV model, if \(R_0\le1\) and the reinfection parameter satisfies \(0<\beta_2\le\beta_2^\ast\), then no positive endemic equilibrium exists; this proves the equilibrium-exclusion part of the paper's Numerical Finding 7.1 and includes the boundary \(R_0=1\).
limitations: Equilibrium exclusion only, not global disease-free convergence.
